source: MCP spec 2026-07-28: pages/specification__2026-07-28__server__utilities__completion.md (full, 217 lines) and pages/specification__2026-07-28__server__utilities__logging.md (full, 135 lines); cross-checked against schema.ts (CompleteRequest, CompleteRequestParams, CompleteResult, CompleteResultResponse, PromptReference, ResourceTemplateReference, Result, ResultType, BaseMetadata, LoggingMessageNotification, LoggingMessageNotificationParams, LoggingLevel, MetaObject key io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel, ServerCapabilities.logging/completions) and pages/specification__2026-07-28__deprecated.md (Logging row); legacy delta cross-checked against 2025-11-25_schema.ts (logging/setLevel, SetLevelRequestParams).
summary: Completion (server/utilities/completion.md): completion/complete (client->server), gated by server ServerCapabilities.completions (JSONObject). params: ref = PromptReference{type:"ref/prompt",name,title?} | ResourceTemplateReference{type:"ref/resource",uri (uri-template)}; argument{name,value}; context?{arguments?:{[k:string]:string}}. Every request's _meta MUST include io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion, clientInfo, clientCapabilities. Result = CompleteResult extends Result: resultType (2026-07-28 servers MUST include it, "complete" for normal completion; absent field from older server MUST be treated as "complete"), completion{values:string[] max 100 items, total?, hasMore?}. Errors SHOULD be -32601/-32602/-32603. Security MUSTs: validate inputs, rate-limit, control access to sensitive suggestions, prevent completion-based info disclosure. Logging (server/utilities/logging.md, DEPRECATED per SEP-2577 as of 2026-07-28): notifications/message (server->client), gated by ServerCapabilities.logging; params{level:LoggingLevel(8 RFC5424 values debug..emergency), logger?, data:unknown}. Major delta: logging/setLevel RPC REMOVED; replaced by per-request _meta key io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel. Server MUST NOT emit notifications/message for a request lacking that key; when present MAY emit at/above that level, strictly on that request's own response stream before its final response, and MUST NOT deliver on subscriptions/listen or any other stream. Security MUST NOTs: no credentials/secrets/PII/attack-aiding internal details in log data. Feature retained >=12 months post-2026-07-28; new implementations SHOULD NOT adopt; migrate to stderr (stdio) or OpenTelemetry.

methods.name: completion/complete
methods.capability_gate: Server MUST declare ServerCapabilities.completions (JSONObject, e.g. {}) to support this method (completion.md L35-45; schema.ts L815). No documented client-side capability requirement.
methods.params: CompleteRequestParams (schema.ts ~L2590-2618): ref: PromptReference{type:"ref/prompt", name:string (required, BaseMetadata), title?:string} | ResourceTemplateReference{type:"ref/resource", uri:string (format uri-template, may be literal URI or template e.g. file:///{path})}. argument (required): {name:string, value:string}. context (optional): {arguments?: {[key:string]:string} — previously-resolved argument name->value map for multi-arg prompts/templates}. Per completion.md Note (L14-21), every request's _meta MUST also include io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities (omitted from page JSON examples only for brevity).
methods.result: CompleteResult extends Result (schema.ts L2644-2661): _meta?:ResultMetaObject; resultType:ResultType (schema.ts L216: "complete"|"input_required"|string) — 2026-07-28 servers MUST include this field (value "complete" for normal completion, per example L81); a client receiving a result from an older server lacking resultType MUST treat it as "complete" (schema.ts L226-233). completion (required object): values:string[] REQUIRED, @maxItems 100 (MUST NOT exceed 100, schema.ts L2646-2650, completion.md L148); total?:number (may exceed values.length); hasMore?:boolean.
methods.notes: Only two ref types exist: ref/prompt and ref/resource. Error handling, server SHOULD (completion.md L187-194): method not found/capability not supported -> -32601; invalid prompt name -> -32602; missing required arguments -> -32602; internal errors -> -32603 (all SHOULD). Implementation considerations (SHOULD/MAY, L196-207): servers SHOULD sort by relevance, fuzzy-match, rate-limit, validate inputs; clients SHOULD debounce, cache, handle partial results gracefully. Security (MUST, L211-216): validate all completion inputs; implement appropriate rate limiting; control access to sensitive suggestions; prevent completion-based information disclosure.

methods.name: notifications/message
methods.capability_gate: Server MUST declare ServerCapabilities.logging (JSONObject, e.g. {}) to emit this notification (logging.md L32-42; schema.ts L808). Entire feature DEPRECATED as of 2026-07-28 (SEP-2577); new implementations SHOULD NOT adopt.
methods.params: LoggingMessageNotificationParams extends NotificationParams (schema.ts L2031-2044): level:LoggingLevel (required); logger?:string (optional logger name); data:unknown (required, any JSON-serializable value/object).
methods.notes: Envelope: {jsonrpc:"2.0", method:"notifications/message", params:{level,logger?,data}} (logging.md L82-98). Emission rules are MUST-level and request-scoped (logging.md L62-74, schema.ts L100-111): server MUST NOT emit for a request whose _meta lacks io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel; when present, server MAY send notifications/message at/above the requested level ONLY on the response stream of that specific request, before its final response; server MUST NOT deliver it on a subscriptions/listen stream or on any other stream.

methods.name: logging/setLevel
methods.capability_gate: Present only in 2025-11-25/2025-06-18 schemas; zero occurrences in 2026-07-28 schema.ts. An SDK targeting 2026-07-28 MUST NOT implement this as a live RPC; retained here only for dual-era support planning.
methods.notes: Superseded by the per-request io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel _meta field (see notifications/message row).

requirements.text: Servers that support completions MUST declare the completions capability.
Every completion/complete request MUST include _meta fields io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities.
completion.values MUST NOT exceed 100 items.
Implementations MUST validate all completion inputs.
Implementations MUST implement appropriate rate limiting for completions.
Implementations MUST control access to sensitive completion suggestions.
Implementations MUST prevent completion-based information disclosure.
Servers SHOULD return -32601 (method not found/capability not supported), -32602 (invalid prompt name; missing required arguments), -32603 (internal error) as appropriate.
Servers SHOULD sort suggestions by relevance, implement fuzzy matching, rate limit requests, validate all inputs.
Clients SHOULD debounce rapid completion requests, cache results, handle missing/partial results gracefully.
Clients SHOULD include previously-resolved argument values in context.arguments for multi-argument prompts/templates.
Servers that emit log message notifications MUST declare the logging capability.
Server MUST NOT emit notifications/message for a request that does not include io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel in that request's _meta.
When io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel is present, server MAY send notifications/message at/above the requested level on that request's response stream, before the final response.
Server MUST NOT deliver notifications/message on a subscriptions/listen stream or on any stream other than the response stream of the request that set the level.
If io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel is not a recognized level, server SHOULD reject the request with -32602; internal errors -> -32603.
Servers SHOULD rate limit log messages, include relevant context in data, use consistent logger names, remove sensitive information.
Clients MAY present log messages in UI, implement filtering/search, display severity visually, persist messages.
Log messages MUST NOT contain credentials/secrets, PII, or internal system details that could aid attacks.
Implementations SHOULD rate limit messages, validate all data fields, control log access, monitor for sensitive content.
New implementations SHOULD NOT adopt the deprecated Logging feature.
Existing implementations SHOULD migrate to stderr logging (stdio) or OpenTelemetry.
2026-07-28 servers MUST include resultType on every Result, including CompleteResult.
Client MUST treat an absent resultType (from an older server) as "complete".

wire_details: ServerCapabilities keys: completions (JSONObject, e.g. {}), logging (JSONObject, e.g. {}).
_meta key: io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel (optional, request-scoped, type LoggingLevel) — per-request logging opt-in, replaces logging/setLevel.
_meta keys required on every request: io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities.
_meta key for subscription-delivered notifications (NOT applicable to notifications/message, which must never use a subscription stream): io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId.
LoggingLevel enum exact values: debug, info, notice, warning, error, critical, alert, emergency (RFC 5424).
ResultType type: "complete" | "input_required" | string (open union); CompleteResult uses "complete".
CompleteResult.completion.total: optional number, may exceed values.length.

JSON-RPC error codes: -32601 (method not found/capability not supported, completion), -32602 (invalid params: invalid prompt name / missing required arguments for completion; invalid/unrecognized logLevel for logging), -32603 (internal error, both).
No HTTP-specific status codes, MIME types, or transport-layer headers documented on either page — both are transport-agnostic message-level specs; no header requirements found in the read material.
sdk_implications: Model CompletionReference as a discriminated union on `type` with exactly two literal tags ("ref/prompt", "ref/resource"); reject any other value client- and server-side.
Implement completion/complete client call requiring/checking server-advertised `completions` capability before calling (or at least surface the server's -32601 cleanly).
Enforce the 100-item cap on completion.values server-side before serialization; truncate and set hasMore=$true (optionally total) rather than emit more than 100.

Build a shared request-envelope helper that stamps every outgoing request's _meta with io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities, rather than re-deriving per call site.

All Result-derived response types (including CompleteResult) must serialize `resultType`; default to "complete" for standard completion responses; on deserialize, coerce a missing resultType (older server) to "complete".
Do NOT implement logging/setLevel as a stateful RPC for 2026-07-28; if dual-protocol support is required, gate it behind negotiated protocolVersion < 2026-07-28.

Implement server-side logging emission as strictly per-request-stream-scoped: read io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel off the current in-flight request's _meta, and only if present allow the handler to write notifications/message frames onto THAT request's own response stream (never a global broadcast bus, never the subscriptions/listen channel).

Validate LoggingLevel against the fixed 8-value set (debug/info/notice/warning/error/critical/alert/emergency); reject unrecognized values and (server-side) prefer emitting -32602 per SHOULD guidance.

Because Logging is deprecated (>=12 months retained from 2026-07-28), surface a deprecation warning (e.g., Write-Warning) when a consumer opts into the logging capability, pointing at stderr/OpenTelemetry as the SHOULD alternative, without removing the feature.

Type LoggingMessageNotificationParams.data as an arbitrary JSON-serializable value (object/array/string), not a fixed schema; provide an injectable sanitizer hook so consumers can strip credentials/secrets/PII/internal details before emission (MUST NOT list).

Expose rate-limiting as pluggable middleware for both completion/complete (server MUST) and log emission (SHOULD both sides) rather than a hardcoded policy, since the spec mandates the outcome but not the mechanism.
legacy_delta: logging/setLevel RPC REMOVED in 2026-07-28: 2025-11-25_schema.ts defines method "logging/setLevel" with SetLevelRequestParams{level:LoggingLevel} and doc comment 'If no logging/setLevel request has been sent from the client, the server MAY decide which messages to send automatically'; grep of 2026-07-28 schema.ts for 'SetLevelRequest|logging/setLevel' returns zero matches (only a reference comment noting it is replaced).

2026-07-28 replaces the persistent/global setLevel model with per-request opt-in via _meta key io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel (schema.ts comment: 'Replaces the former logging/setLevel RPC'). Delivery becomes strictly request-scoped: MUST NOT emit without the field; MUST NOT deliver on subscriptions/listen or any stream other than the triggering request's own response stream (logging.md L65-74) — materially different from the prior persistent/global channel where, once armed via setLevel, the server could push notifications/message at any time on any channel.

Whole Logging feature (capability, notifications/message, LoggingLevel, logLevel meta key) newly marked @deprecated as of 2026-07-28 per SEP-2577 (schema.ts L2049-2051, L2069-2071; logging.md L9-19); feature-lifecycle policy keeps it in spec >=12 months post-2026-07-28 (deprecated.md: removal-eligible 'First revision released on or after 2027-07-28'). New implementations SHOULD NOT adopt; existing SHOULD migrate to stderr (stdio transport) or OpenTelemetry.

CompleteResult gains a MUST-include `resultType` field in 2026-07-28 (inherited from the generic Result base, schema.ts L223-235), shown in the completion.md example ("resultType":"complete"). Backward-compat rule: client receiving a result without resultType (older server) MUST treat it as "complete".

completion.md's Note asserts every 2026-07-28 request MUST carry _meta keys io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities — a per-request re-statement of identity/version/capabilities not present in the same mandatory form in prior revisions (there, negotiation happened once at initialize). This delta is asserted only by the completion page's note; the underlying basic/index#meta page itself was not read in this task, so the precise scope needs direct verification (see open_questions).
open_questions: Exact field name(s) inside ResultMetaObject carrying server-identification info (grep hit around schema.ts L136-150 was truncated mid-sentence: 'Servers SHOULD include this field on every response...') — needs a direct read of schema.ts L136-160 plus the basic/index page to confirm the precise _meta key (likely io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo or similar) before finalizing SDK response envelope types.

The basic/index page's _meta section (referenced by completion.md's Note) was not read in this task; the exact required shape/types of io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities, and whether they are MUST on literally every request method or only some, should be verified directly rather than inferred solely from the completion page's note.

Whether ServerCapabilities.logging / completions (typed as plain JSONObject) can carry any documented optional sub-fields beyond an empty baseline example was not fully cross-checked against 2026-07-28_schema.json; schema.ts shows no named properties for either.

CompleteRequestParams.context.arguments is typed {[key:string]:string} (string-only values) in schema.ts; not cross-checked against 2026-07-28_schema.json for stricter/looser validation — confirm before codegen of strict PowerShell parameter validation.

No explicit spec text found establishing whether completion/complete for a ref/resource requires the server to also advertise a resources/resource-templates capability; this cross-dependency (or its absence) should be confirmed against the resources page before an SDK adds any client-side pre-check/warning.
